findings.text: A mark in a glossary entry's Deviations field now makes the entry depend on the marked term, so Deviations count as meaning-bearing. But change_effects gives "dependents" only for a changed Definition or Defined by: a reworded Deviations field changes the term's meaning, yet no rule marking that term is listed as changed through it.

A definition may now mark an open term and stays to be built. So a rule marking a defined term whose Definition marks an open term is to be built, although its meaning depends on an undecided one. lint.undecided.term holds a rule undecided for exactly that, but only through a direct mark, and no rule decides the indirect case beyond the open term itself being reported.

The When step reads marks "of the capability <capability>", but a Definition or Deviations field of a system glossary entry belongs to no capability. Only the Examples row with capability "the system" covers it, so the step does not say which glossaries a system-level mark may resolve to.

The rule block's Then step names every chain that reaches an element, and only the Rationale and one Examples row say a chain passes no element twice. That row covers only a circle that contains the changed element. Nothing decides the case where entries A and B mark each other and A marks a changed C. A is listed through C, but it is unclear whether A is also named through the chain C, A, B, which comes back to A. It is also unclear whether 'passes twice' counts the element the chain reaches.
